title: Mark the Soft-falling Snow
description: Mark the Soft-falling Snow in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 293 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Efficacy of the Gospel”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Mark the soft fall-ing snow, And the de-scend-ing rain! To heaven, from whence it fell, It turns not back a-gain; But wa-ters earth through ev-ery pore, And calls forth all her se-cret store.

lines: To heaven, from whence it fell,
But waters earth through every pore,
And calls forth all her secret store.
And man and beast are fed
The harvest bows its golden ears,
The copious seed of future years.
Millions of souls shall feel its power,
And bear it down to millions more."

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
